definition: The Hessian affine region detector is a feature detector used in the fields of computer vision and image analysis.
details: Like other feature detectors, the Hessian affine detector is typically used as a preprocessing step to algorithms that rely on identifiable, characteristic interest points. The Hessian affine detector is part of the subclass of feature detectors known as affine-invariant detectors: Harris affine region detector, Hessian affine regions, maximally stable extremal regions, Kadir–Brady saliency detector, edge-based regions (EBR) and intensity-extrema-based (IBR) regions.
story: Picture walking through a crowd and instantly picking out a familiar face without reading a single name tag. The machine learns to see the way we do — starting with shapes and edges, then building up to whole objects and faces. It turns a picture into an understanding: this is a cat, that is a stop sign. Sight, for a machine, is a long climb from raw light to a name. That pixel-to-meaning climb is Hessian affine region detector.
